_readme: Grammatical error correction with Unbabel/gec-t5_small, run on this machine. Read by tools/gec.py and by the CLI chat's opt-in second opinion. There is deliberately no 'enabled' switch here: the model is never on the default reply path, because the APK and the web page are stdlib/browser-only and cannot load a T5. Turning it on is a per-invocation choice (FLUENTIFY_GEC=1) so the shipped chat, the JS port and the parity suites cannot drift.

model._readme: The checkpoint from the model card. gec-t5_small is T5-small fine-tuned on the BEA-2019 / CoNLL / FCE corpora; apache-2.0, ~242 MB of fp32 weights.

run._readme: Generation settings from the model card, with one addition: no_repeat_ngram_size, because a 60M-parameter model can otherwise loop on an unusual word.

env._readme: Where the weights live when they have been fetched, and the interpreter that holds torch/transformers. Both are outside git.

notes.network: Only the first run downloads the checkpoint. After that every correction is computed on this device.
notes.surfaces: CLI, and the web preview through POST-free /api/correct (the pen button in the composer). The chat replies are untouched - the model answers a question about one sentence - and the APK keeps the rule-based checker in bot.js, which is what ships.
